title: triage-kernel-todo-rajiv
content:
2026-03-13 morning notes - quick brain dump

Primary focus: triage high-severity regressions from last deploy, isolate KV-cache-induced 99p latency spikes, get a minimal repro for kernel preemption issue. Keep everything lightweight — notes to self rather than polished doc.

OVERVIEW / CONTEXT:
- Yesterday's deploy (canary -> all) bumped runtime to v1.14.0; saw 3 customer incidents with tail latency regressions (p99 up from ~820ms -> ~1.3s on long-context routes).
- Suspect interaction between continuous batching adjustments + new LRU eviction tweak in kv-cache. Also seeing occasional "kernel preempted while holding page lock" in node logs (rare).
- Priority: get reproducible local case, triage whether kv-cache is root cause, add temporary mitigation (reduce per-batch size / increase cache TTL) while we fix.

MORNING TRIAGE LIST (ordered):
1) Collect traces for 3 incidents (RR-1789) - Mina has first-hand trace links.
   - Action: download trace bundles -> /tmp/rr1789-traces.tar.gz
   - Slack Mina for missing spans: @mina - ask for full sampling traces for affected routes.
2) Reproduce p99 spike locally with load generator (simulate long prompt, seq_len ~2048).
   - quick command: ./bench/run_chat_load.sh --clients 20 --seq 2048 --model rwd-open-13b --batch 1 --duration 5m
   - if no spike, try with continuous-batching enabled + cache warmup disabled (to simulate cold-cache write patterns).
3) Reproduce kernel message: grep logs for "preempted while holding page lock" across nodes from 03/12 22:00-02:00UTC.
   - grep -R "preempted while holding page lock" /var/log/redwood/* | sed -n '1,200p'
4) Rollback plan ready: pin runtime to v1.13.7 in canary pool config if we cannot triage within 2 hours.

QUICK OBSERVATIONS / RAW METRICS (from morning checks):
- Canary p50: 120ms (ok), p95: 540ms (slightly up), p99: 1.28s (regression).
- KV-cache hit rate for affected routes: 0.67 -> baseline was ~0.81.
- Batching size distribution shifted: more small batches (<4) after change to batching heuristic.
- Node OOMs: none. CPU spikes align with p99 windows on worker-gpu-03.

HYPOTHESES (ranked):
A) LRU eviction/tuning in kv-cache is evicting hot prefixes prematurely when batching behavior changes -> increases backend work and tail latency.
B) Kernel preemption log is symptom of long syscalls (disk or mmap) under heavy concurrent KV writes -> contends with page lock.
C) New batching heuristic increases number of cold cache lookups per second -> amplifies KV write traffic -> backend throttling at PCIe/NVMe level.

REPRO STEPS (what I'll run now):
- Start a controlled load against local runtime with exactly the same route header, session id pattern as prod incidents (simulate many short-lived sessions):
  - curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/predict -d @long_prompt.json -H 'Authorization: Bearer local' -H 'x-session-id: seq-$R'
- Toggle caching: set REDWOOD_KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=5000 and run bench.
- Toggle batching: ENV CONT_BS_HEURISTIC=legacy and run bench.
- Kernel repro: run 50 concurrent small file mmaps + heavy KV writes to see if holding-page-lock shows up: tiny test harness in /tmp/page_lock_test.c

KERNEL/OS NOTES:
- Message observed: "task xyz preempted while holding page lock" — likely kernel WARNING from mm/mmap.c. Might occur when an mmap munmap sequence races with page reclaim.
- Quick check: Are we hitting any large munmap() or madvise() calls in runtime on eviction path? Search for munmap in repo:
  - rg "munmap|madvise" -S
- Thought: if eviction is synchronous and calls munmap on large backing regions while holding global mutex, can cause lengthy syscall -> kernel warns. Consider making eviction async or off-thread.

MINI EXPERIMENTS (notes):
- Local bench w/ legacy batching + cache max=10k: p99 ~ 880-940ms (improved).
- Local bench w/ new batching + cache max=5k: p99 ~1.2s and cache hit 0.62 (worse).
- Observation: enabling async-evict (branch: rajiv/async-evict) drops eviction syscall time in perf traces. Need to profile more.

SHORT-TERM MITIGATION (1-3 hours):
- Increase cache TTL for long-context routes (config route-match: ":/chat/long") -> set TTL 600s.
- Revert continuous-batching heuristic for canary nodes (reconfigure via rollout).
- Add temporary rate-limit on KV write path (throttle writes from batching collector).

TODO (actionable, owner, eta):
- [ ] Get Mina's full spans + perf flamegraphs for incidents (Mina) - ETA 1h.
- [ ] Run controlled repro with env toggles and attach flamegraphs (Rajiv) - ETA 2h.
- [ ] Open minimal PR to make eviction async if perf confirms syscall block (Rajiv) - ETA EOD.
- [ ] Draft rollback note and coordinate with SRE for pinning runtime (Samira) - ETA 30m.
- [ ] Add e2e test that simulates mmapped eviction + continuous batching for CI (owner: Eng test infra) - ETA next sprint.

QUESTIONS / THINGS TO CHECK WITH TEAM:
- Does anyone remember why we made eviction synchronous originally? (cost model?)
- Is there a known kernel-bug (we're on Ubuntu 22.04 kernel 5.15) with this page-lock message? Quick web search didn't show matching open bugs.
- Can platform SRE disable new batching heuristic in the 1.14 canary group quickly? Samira said yes but want confirmation.

NOTES TO SELF / MEETING POINTS:
- If repro reproduces in 30m -> signal rollback. No need to escalate to execs yet.
- Keep customer comms short: "We're investigating tail latency regression; mitigation in progress; ETA 2 hours for rollback if needed." (CS template).

RANDOM COMMANDS / SNIPPETS I KEEP USING:
- tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | rg "p99|preempted|evict"
- sudo perf record -g -p $(pidof redwood-runtime) -- sleep 30; sudo perf report
- ./bench/run_chat_load.sh --clients 20 --seq 2048 --duration 5m --env OVERRIDE=CONT_BS_HEURISTIC=legacy

ENDPOINTS / DASHBOARDS TO CHECK:
- https://grafana.redwood.local/d/runtime/latency?var-model=rwd-open-13b
- traces: https://jaeger.redwood.local/trace/rr-1789

BACKLOG IDEAS (not now):
- Add eviction metrics (time spent per munmap, bytes freed) and a histogram for eviction syscall latency.
- Consider mmapped region pooling to avoid frequent munmap/mmap churn.
- Revisit batching heuristic to prefer slightly larger batches at low concurrency.

FINAL: will update this doc with repro artifacts + PR links. If Mina posts spans, I'll paste them here.

---

Notes to self at 11:45am: started local bench, p99 trending down with legacy heuristic — good sign. Next step: push small PR to toggle async-evict flag behind feature-flag and run A/B in canary.
